Question_text: Chung is a trader who buys and sells on cash and credit terms. He provided the following information for April 2017. April 1 Chung owed Delun, a credit supplier, $1500. 10 Chung purchased goods on credit from Delun, list price $1400, less 20% trade discount. 15 Chung returned to Delun some of the goods purchased on 10 April, list price $200. 23 Chung paid the balance owed to Delun at 1 April by cheque and was allowed 2% cash discount. REQUIRED (a) Prepare the account of Delun in the ledger of Chung for April 2017. Balance the account and bring down the balance on 1 May 2017. (b) State the sub-division of Chung's ledger which would contain the account of Delun. (c) Name the document that was issued by Delun to Chung on the following dates. April 10 Chung purchased goods on credit from Delun. April 15 Chung returned to Delun some of the goods purchased on 10 April. (d) Name the document which Delun may issue to Chung on 30 April 2017. (e) Complete the table to state the effect of each of the following transactions made by Chung in April 2017. Where there is no effect write ‘No effect'. The first transaction has been completed as an example. (f) State two reasons why book-keeping records are maintained.
Unit: UNIT 2: Sources and recording of data
Topic: 2.1 The double entry system of book-keeping

Question_text: Umar sells goods on credit and maintains a sales ledger control account. The following information is available for the month ended 31 March 2017. REQUIRED (a) State two benefits of using control accounts. (b) Prepare the sales ledger control account for March 2017. Balance the account and bring down the balance on 1 April 2017. (c) Prepare the provision for doubtful debts account for the year ended 31 March 2017. Balance the account and bring down the balance on 1 April 2017. (d) Name one accounting concept or principle that supports the use of a provision for doubtful debts. (e) Prepare the journal entry made by Umar to record the bankruptcy of Horner. A narrative is required.
